chunk_findings.detail: The diff changes the MCP JSON body serialization from `json.dumps(..., indent=2)` to `json.dumps(full, separators=(",", ":"), ...)` for *every* outcome, not just the bounded reads. The surrounding comment still asserts the MCP/CLI contract "The CLI's `--json` is the whole body; the two differ only here" (i.e. only by the bound). But after this change MCP and CLI differ in *formatting* as well: for any tool whose MCP body is currently byte-identical to the CLI `--json` (the parity tests the acceptance criterion says must "stay green"), the MCP `content[0]` is now compact while the CLI `--json` (unchanged, still `indent=2`) is not, so `json.loads(mcp_body) == json.loads(cli_json)` may hold but the byte-identity assertion fails. Concretely, a tool like `decide`/`show` whose parity test does `assert mcp_result.content[0] == cli_json_output` will now compare `{"a":1}` against `{\n  "a": 1\n}` and fail. Either the CLI must also compact (which contradicts the stated "--json unchanged") or the compaction must be scoped to the projected tools only, as B-fix-status-bound did; as written, part 2 applies it unconditionally.

chunk_findings.detail: The truncation note is appended to `result["content"]` *before* the reason block, so when a bounded read both truncates and has `out.reason`, `content` becomes `[body, note, reason, ...]`. The comment on the reason branch documents it as "A SECOND content block, never a prefix", i.e. `content[1]` is the reason; with a note present a consumer that reads `content[1]` as the reason now gets the truncation note instead. The note should be appended after the reason (or the reason contract updated) so the documented position of the reason is preserved for truncating outcomes that also carry a reason.
chunk_findings.title: surfaces/mcp.py:_outcome_result (note block, ~line 2781)

chunk_findings.detail: `bound_recall` unconditionally strips every hit's `raw` field (`hit = {k: v for k, v in hits[rank].items() if k != "raw"}`), but the disclosure for that projection (`raw = "each hit's raw record is left out..."`) is only returned when the answer was also truncated. Given input that fits the budget — e.g. `body = {"facts": [{"id": "a", "kind": "fact", "headline": "h", "body": "b", "raw": {...}}]}` with the default `max_chars=4000` — `shown == total`, so `note` is `None`, and the function returns `(out, None)`. The MCP body therefore has `raw` removed with no `truncated` field and no second content block, while the CLI `--json` body still contains `raw`. This contradicts the module's own stated rule ("Nothing is dropped silently") and the stated invariant that the MCP body and `--json` "agree only while nothing crosses a bound": here no bound was crossed, yet the two bodies differ, and the projection is invisible to the caller. The fix is to emit the `raw` disclosure even when nothing was truncated (i.e. always produce a note), not only in the `shown < total` branch.

chunk_findings.detail: The new truncation note is appended to `result["content"]` *before* the `out.reason` block, so for any bounded tool that both truncates and carries a reason the content array changes from `[body, reason, ...]` to `[body, note, reason, ...]`. The reason block's own contract in this same function is "A SECOND content block" (i.e. `content[1]`), and the comment for the footer explicitly says content is ordered so that the answer stays at `content[0]` and the reason follows it immediately. Concrete scenario: call `next` (or `progress`/`decision_list`) on a repository large enough to be truncated where the outcome also sets `out.reason` (e.g. the "N items blocked"/gates summary). Before this change a caller that reads `result["content"][1]["text"]` gets the reason; now it gets the truncation note instead, and the reason moves to `content[2]`. Any test or `jtool`-style consumer that reads the reason by position (not by scanning all blocks) will now either fail or report the wrong text. The note should be appended after the `if out.reason:` block so the reason keeps its established slot.

chunk_findings.detail: The top-level projection line `out = {k: v for k, v in _lean(body).items() if v is not False and k not in ITEM_PLUMBING}` drops `landed_before`/`landed_after` (and every `False`-valued field) but never records this in `stripped` or `cut[0]`. `stripped` is only set inside the gate-evidence loop, and `cut[0]` only counts clipped gate/triage strings, so the `truncated` marker (`if stripped or cut[0]: ...`) is not emitted in this case. Concrete input: a `ddflow_show` body for a merged item that carries `landed_before`/`landed_after` (the exact fields `ITEM_PLUMBING` targets), whose gates either are absent or contain no `GATE_BOILERPLATE` keys, and whose gate/triage strings are all ≤ `TEXT_SHOWN`. The output has both plumbing fields removed but no `truncated` key at all, contradicting the module's own rule that "a list that is cut says so" / "Nothing is dropped silently." The same hole applies to `if v is not False`, which also contradicts `_lean`'s stated "False and 0 are real answers and stay" — top-level `False` fields vanish with no marker.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_show

chunk_findings.detail: This unconditionally appends `"Z"` after truncating on the first `.`, so it is only correct when the timestamp contains a fractional-second part. Given a gate record whose `at` has no fractional seconds — e.g. `"2024-01-01T10:00:00Z"` or `"2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00"` (older/truncated records, or anything written with `timespec="seconds"`) — `partition(".")[0]` returns the whole string and the result becomes `"2024-01-01T10:00:00ZZ"` or `"2024-01-01T10:00:00+00:00Z"`, a malformed timestamp. When a fractional part is present but the offset is non-UTC (e.g. `"...T10:00:00.123456+05:00"`), the offset is discarded and replaced with `Z`, shifting the represented time by five hours.

chunk_findings.detail: The change's report measures the pre-change MCP bodies as next 35,189 B, show 11,412 B, recall 32,454 B, decision_list 39,948 B, progress 149,575 B. The README, which the acceptance criterion requires to "record before/after", gives a different set of before numbers: next 33 KB, show 8.9 KB, `recall` 49 KB, decision_list 44 KB, progress 152 KB. The recall figure is off by ~17 KB (32,454 B ≈ 31.7 KiB, not 49 KB), and decision_list/progress/show are each several KB off, so the "before" column in the README does not reproduce the measurements the change claims to have made on this repository. Either the README numbers or the reported measurements are wrong; given the acceptance requires the before/after to be "recorded in the report", wrong numbers here make the documented evidence for the 50% reduction claim unusable even though the reduction itself is satisfied. (I could not verify the code paths themselves — parts 2–5 of the diff were not provided — so I make no claim about the actual MCP behavior beyond this textual contradiction.)

chunk_findings.detail: The MCP body is now serialized with `json.dumps(full, separators=(",", ":"))` while the CLI `--json` path (per the very comment this hunk rewrites: "MCP encodes it compact, the CLI indented") still emits `indent=2`. The comment used to pin the invariant "the two are byte-identical"; the hunk silently downgrades that to "same parsed body" without changing the CLI side, so the two surfaces are no longer byte-identical for *any* JSON tool — not just the deliberately projected ones. Concretely: call any JSON tool (e.g. `decide`, `load`, or the unbounded `show` before its bound applies) over MCP and read `content[0].text`; it is now a single-line compact encoding, whereas the same `Outcome.body(payload_key)` rendered via `--json` is multi-line indented text. A pre-existing parity test that asserts textual equality between the MCP body and the CLI `--json` output (the property the old comment and the change's own acceptance criterion — "the CLI --json stays byte-identical to the MCP body wherever tests pin parity", "the parity tests ... stay green" — describe) now fails, and the only thing that changed is a doc comment asserting the divergence is fine.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:2774 (`_outcome_result`)

chunk_findings.detail: `bound_recall` guarantees the first hit of every kind is kept regardless of `max_chars`, and the budget check `if rank and used + size > budget: continue` never runs for `rank == 0`, so `max_chars` is not enforced for one hit per kind. Worse, when every kind has exactly one hit, `shown == total`, so no truncation note is emitted at all and the caller cannot tell the budget was ignored. Concretely, with a body of seven kinds, each holding a single hit whose headline+body is ~3000 chars, and `args = {"max_chars": 1}`, `_limit`-equivalent parsing yields `budget = 1`, all seven rank-0 hits are appended, `shown = 7 == total`, and the function returns ~21 KB of hits plus the note "each hit's raw record is left out" — no `truncated` text, silently exceeding the requested budget by four orders of magnitude. Even in the case where truncation is reported, the message `f"truncated: showing {shown} of {total} hits within max_chars={budget}"` is false for exactly the same reason (the always-kept first hits are not counted against the stated bound), so the note asserts a limit that the output violates.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_recall

chunk_findings.detail: `bound_show` removes and rewrites fields that are not reflected in the `truncated` metadata, contradicting the module docstring's "Nothing is dropped silently" rule and its `left_out` enumeration (`"gate evidence tree ids, landed_before/after"`). Specifically, `one = {k: v for k, v in rec.items() if k != "gate"}` drops the per-gate `gate` key, `one["at"] = _FRACTION.sub("Z", one["at"])` rewrites timestamps, and `rec.pop("location", None)` deletes a triage `location` key — none of these touch `stripped` or `cut[0]`. Given a body such as `{"state": "done", "gates": {"g": {"gate": "g", "at": "2024-01-01T00:00:00.123Z", "witness": "ok"}}, "triage": {"t": {"title": "T", "location": "T"}}}`, the returned record has no `gate` key, `at == "2024-01-01T00:00:00Z"`, and no `location`, yet `stripped` is `False` and `cut[0]` is `0`, so no `truncated` field is added and a consumer is told (by omission) that the record is complete.

chunk_findings.detail: The `max_chars` budget is measured only as `len(headline) + len(body)` per hit, and rank-0 hits bypass the check entirely (`if rank and used + size > budget`). The returned body is therefore a full JSON object per hit (id, kind, timestamp, every non-`raw` field, plus JSON overhead), so the actual payload can be an order of magnitude over the advertised bound while the emitted note asserts it stayed within it. Concrete input: `max_chars=4000` and a single kind with 5000 hits of `{"id":"...","headline":"x","body":"y"}`. `used` reaches 4000 after ~2000 hits, so 2000 hits are kept and the note reads "showing 2000 of 5000 hits within max_chars=4000" — but 2000 serialized hits are ~80 KB, not 4000 bytes. This is the number the note hands to the caller/model and the property the recall bound is supposed to guarantee; here it is simply false. (The docstring likewise claims the whole hit is "within max_chars", which the code does not implement.)
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_recall

chunk_findings.detail: `bound_show` mutates content without recording it in `truncated`, contradicting "Nothing is dropped silently." Two concrete cases: (1) `_FRACTION.sub("Z", one["at"])` rewrites gate timestamps, and neither `stripped` nor `cut[0]` is set for it — input `{"state":"x","gates":{"lint":{"gate":"lint","at":"2024-01-01T00:00:00.500Z","evidence":{"ok":true}}}}` (no boilerplate keys, no string over `TEXT_SHOWN`) returns `at = "...T00:00:00Z"` with no `truncated` field at all, so the MCP body silently differs from `--json next`/`show` and from any gate whose `at` ended in `.100Z`. (2) The triage cleanup runs *after* `_clip`, so it compares already-truncated values: for a record with `title = "A"*300` and `location = "A"*205 + "B"`, both collapse to `"A"*200 + " [...]"`, `rec.get("location") == rec.get("title")` is True, and `location` is popped even though it originally differed from `title` — again with no entry in `truncated`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_show

chunk_findings.detail: The previous code emitted `json.dumps(..., indent=2, ...)` and the docstring guaranteed that the MCP body was byte-identical to the CLI's `--json`, which the intent says is to remain unchanged ("the CLI --json stays byte-identical to the MCP body wherever tests pin parity"). This hunk changes the MCP side to compact separators for *all* JSON tools, not just the bounded reads, while the CLI `--json` path is untouched and still indented. Given a fixed repo state, `mcp_..._call(...)["content"][0]["text"]` and the CLI `--json` stdout for the same tool now differ wherever whitespace exists (e.g. compact `{"rows":[...]}` vs indented `{\n  "rows": [...]`). The docstring was reworded to "the same parsed body", but that is a redefinition of the guarantee the acceptance text pins ("the parity tests ... stay green"). Any test or consumer that compares the two bodies as text (the property the old "byte-identical" wording documented) now fails for every JSON tool, including the unbounded ones that were never supposed to change encoding. If the parity tests indeed compare parsed values this is harmless, but the change as written drops a documented byte-identity guarantee for the entire JSON surface rather than only the deliberately-projected bounded reads.

chunk_findings.detail:
In `bound_show`, the triage loop pops `location` when it duplicates `title` with:

```python
if isinstance(rec, dict) and rec.get("location") == rec.get("title"):
    rec.pop("location", None)
    stripped = True
```

When a triage record carries neither key, `rec.get("location")` and `rec.get("title")` are both `None`, and `None == None` is `True`. The pop is then a no-op, but `stripped = True` is still set. For a `ddflow_show` body whose triage contains any such record (and with no gates/plumbing to justify it), the function returns `out` with a `truncated` object whose `strings_cut` is `0` and whose `left_out` claims "tree ids, gate names, sub-second times, landed_before/after" were removed — even though nothing was actually removed. That contradicts the module's own "counts are exact" rule and can mislead a consumer into believing the item was projected when it was returned whole. The guard should require the field to be present (e.g. `rec.get("location") is not None and rec["location"] == rec["title"]`) before setting `stripped`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:bound_show (triage dedup)

chunk_findings.detail: The condition `rec.get("location") == rec.get("title")` is true whenever both keys are absent, because `None == None`. Any triage record that carries neither `location` nor `title` (e.g. a session/phase-level note such as `{"note": "..."}`) reaches this line, `rec.pop("location", None)` removes nothing, and `stripped` is set to `True`. That forces the `if stripped or cut[0]:` branch to attach a `truncated` object to the result: `{"strings_cut": 0, "left_out": "tree ids, gate names, sub-second times, landed_before/after", "all": ...}` even though no gate, no `landed_*`, no long string, and no duplicated location were actually omitted. Concretely, for a show body with `triage = {"phase": {"r1": {"note": "x"}}}` and no `gates`, the MCP body gains a `truncated` field the full `--json` body does not have. This both misreports "what was left out" (violating the "truncation is explicit / never silent" contract in the opposite direction) and can break a parity/`test_mcp_payload_bound` assertion that pins MCP == `--json` for items that cross no bound. The check should require the key to be present, e.g. `rec.get("location") is not None and rec.get("location") == rec.get("title")`.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py:142 (`bound_show`, triage dedup)

chunk_findings.detail: This hunk changes the serialization of *every* JSON MCP body from `json.dumps(..., indent=2)` to `json.dumps(..., separators=(",", ":"))`, while the CLI `--json` path is not touched anywhere in this diff. Before this change the module's own contract was that the MCP text and the CLI `--json` text are byte-identical (`Outcome.body` is the one projection "shared with the CLI's `--json` ... the two are byte-identical"); the code comment is edited to weaken this to "the same parsed body", but nothing in the change makes the CLI output compact to match. Concrete demonstration: for any JSON tool that is *not* one of the five deliberately projected reads (e.g. `decide`/`status`/`add`), the MCP result is now `{"a":1}` while the CLI `--json` for the same outcome is `{\n  "a": 1\n}` — the two strings no longer compare equal. Any parity/`test_api_layer` assertion that compares `content[0]["text"]` to the CLI serialization (which the previous docstring advertised as the whole point of the shared `Outcome.body`) now fails, contradicting the acceptance criterion "the parity tests and test_api_layer stay green". The correct shape, per the intent ("the CLI `--json` stays byte-identical to the MCP body wherever tests pin parity ... document where the MCP body is deliberately a projection"), is either to compact both encodings or to restrict the compact/projection change to the five bounded tools rather than applying it unconditionally at the single shared serialization point.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp.py:~2777 (`json.dumps(full, separators=(",", ":"), default=str)` in `_outcome_result`)

chunk_findings.detail: The budget is a single global counter with an unconditional "keep the very first hit" escape, so one hit larger than the budget starves every other kind. Given a recall body whose first iterated hit projects to more than `max_chars` (the default `RECALL_BUDGET = 4000`, easy to hit since a projected hit includes its `body` text), the sequence is: `used == 0`, so `if used and used + size > budget` is False and the hit is kept, making `used` e.g. 5000. For every subsequent hit the guard `used and used + size > budget` is now `5000 and … > 4000` → True, so it executes `continue` unconditionally. Result: the output contains that one kind only; all other six kinds are returned as empty lists, and the note reads `truncated: showing 1 of N hits within max_chars=4000`. This directly contradicts the function's own docstring ("taken one per kind in turn so no source is crowded out") and the stated requirement to cap recall per kind — a single large hit crowds out every other source, and the round-robin never even reaches rank 1.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/surfaces/mcp_bound.py `bound_recall`

chunk_findings.detail: The projected body is rebuilt from scratch keeping only top-level keys whose value is a list, so any non-list top-level field is discarded with no marker. Input `{"hits": [ {...} ], "total": 12}` yields `{"hits": [ ... ]}` — `"total"` is gone and the second content block only says `each hit's raw record is left out (its id is in the hit)`, so the omission of `"total"` (or any error/query/echo field) is silent. This violates the module docstring's "Nothing is dropped silently"; the sibling tools (`bound_progress`/`bound_decisions`) return the body untouched when it is not the expected list shape, so recall is the one place where arbitrary top-level data is silently removed.

chunk_findings.detail: `_clip` returns `value[:TEXT_SHOWN].rstrip() + " [...]"`, i.e. up to `TEXT_SHOWN` characters plus the 6‑character marker `" [...]"`. For any string whose length is in `[TEXT_SHOWN+1, TEXT_SHOWN+6]` = `[161, 166]`, the "clipped" result is **longer** than the original. For example a 161‑character gate‑evidence string becomes `value[:160] + " [...]"` = 166 characters, a net +5 bytes, and `cut[0]` is incremented so it is reported in `truncated.strings_cut` as though it were shortened. Since the whole point of this module is to reduce MCP bytes, the projection can increase the size of the field (and the note claims a shortening that did not happen) for that input window; the marker should be budgeted inside `TEXT_SHOWN`.

chunk_findings.detail: The change swaps the MCP JSON encoder from `json.dumps(..., indent=2)` to `json.dumps(..., separators=(",", ":"))` while the CLI `--json` path still serializes the same `Outcome.body` with indentation. The function's own comment (before this edit) states the preserved property is that the MCP body and the CLI `--json` are *byte-identical*, and the acceptance criteria in the intent require the parity tests to stay green. Because the encoder is now different, that byte identity is necessarily broken for every JSON-valued tool. Concrete example: invoking the `next` tool over MCP now returns a single-line body `{"items":[...],"blocked":{...,"truncated":true}}`, whereas `ddflow next --json` from the same repo returns the same parsed value with `\n  ` indentation; any test or consumer that compares the two result strings (which is precisely what the previous "byte-identical" invariant implies) now fails on whitespace alone. The rewritten comment ("the two are the same parsed body ... not the text") documents the deviation, but it does not make the pinned byte-parity hold, so either the CLI `--json` must also be made compact (contradicting "the CLI --json stays byte-identical"/62 KB) or the parity assertion is now red.

chunk_findings.detail: `bound_decisions` clips the decision text with the guard `if isinstance(text, str) and len(text) > DECISION_TEXT_SHOWN:` and then emits `text[:DECISION_TEXT_SHOWN].rstrip() + " [...]"`. The marker is six characters, so for inputs in `(DECISION_TEXT_SHOWN, DECISION_TEXT_SHOWN + 6]`, i.e. decision texts of 401–406 characters, the "clipped" value is *longer* than the original: `bound_decisions([{"decision": "x"*401, ...}], {})` returns a 406-character `decision` where the caller passed 401. The module's own `_clip` helper documents the correct rule around the same constant (`if len(value) <= TEXT_SHOWN + len(CUT_MARK): return value`, with a comment "Only when the cut is a saving"), so this branch contradicts the projection's stated purpose of reducing bytes and should use the same `+ len(CUT_MARK)` guard (or call `_clip`). Impact is small (a 5-byte growth on a narrow length band) but it is a real divergence from the declared behavior.
